[IsAdicComplete I R]` (FormalGroup/FormalExpHom.lean:48-49, 173). what_it_would_need: To become an input to ANY seed obligation the lead would need theorems that do not exist at the pin and are not about Lean packaging: (1) for the derivative criterion (δ_p ≠ 0, m_p − w_p ≤ 1 ⇒ Ш[p^∞] = 0; w_p = min_i v_p(log_ω(P_i)/p)): a formalized p-adic logarithm on E_1(Q_p) with convergence on pZ_p and the valuation statement v_p(log_ω(P)) = v_p(z(P)) for p > 2 (Silverman AEC IV.6.4b over Z_p, i.e. the p-adic denominator estimate v(n) ≤ log_p n on the coefficients of log_E) — the pinned `formalLogHom`/`formalExpAddEquiv` are stated only for ℚ-algebras and cannot be instantiated at R = Z_p; then, separately, the actual Kato-derivative inputs A_p, B_p, κ(P_i) and the cofinite nonvanishing / excess-content estimate, none of which is local formal-group material. (2) For the remainder primes 2243, 4547, 5843 (B.18) and lemma TH at 5843: production symbols / level-raised theta elements, Bullach–Honnor-type or Fornea–Gehrmann hypotheses — no formal-group or Tate-curve module touches them; the Tate uniformization at the multiplicative primes 3, 2243, 5843 would only re-derive c_p ∈ {1,2} / split vs nonsplit facts already retained (and carries the undischarged `hmem` hypothesis). (3) For ORDER9/Q36: nothing; these need a global size/support bound or a rank-two leading-term formula. (4) For cost reduction: none; the computations are Ota witnesses c_2(θ_ℓ), B.18 symbols, c_1(λ_ℓ), Shii's Fitting comparison — none is a formal-group evaluation. Even the honest reuse (Lean statement of E_1(Q_p) ≅ Ê(pZ_p) and prime-to-p torsion-freeness) would require: fetching and building the pinned package (a dependency build CLAUDE.md forbids starting for this purpose), `#print axioms` on the exact targets, and a hypothesis match (IsIntegral R W for the seed's minimal model at each p; W.IsElliptic).
new_observation: NEW (not in Codex, not in the Oct-6 audit, not in sweep-lean.json): the pinned library's evaluated formal logarithm is structurally unavailable at the seed's primes. FormalLogHom.lean:79-80 and FormalExpHom.lean:48-49 bind `[Algebra ℚ R] ... [IsAdicComplete I R]`; a mixed-characteristic complete DVR such as Z_p is not a ℚ-algebra (p is not invertible), and the only ℚ-algebras that are I-adically complete for I ≠ 0 are equal-characteristic-zero rings like Q[[t]]. So at this pin `log_E : Ê(𝔪) → 𝔾_a` and `Ê(𝔪) ≅ 𝔪` (Silverman IV.6.4a/b) are formalized ONLY in equal characteristic zero; the p-adic case that the lab's w_p = min v_p(log_ω(P_i)/p) uses — convergence of log_E on pZ_p and v_p(log_E(z)) = v_p(z) for p > 2 — is absent, and no FormalGroup/ module name at the pin (57 files; tree listing truncated:false) suggests a p-adic/Z_p variant. Codex's §3 item 1 'Reuse: formal checks of the seed local-log normalization ... could reuse this algebra' therefore overstates: only the series identity log∘[n] = n·log is reusable, and it is a ℚ-algebra statement that says nothing about Z_p-valuations. The one module that does admit Z_p is E₁AddEquiv (no ℚ-algebra hypothesis), together with E₁_eq_zero_of_isUnit_nsmul; both are abstract group statements with no logarithm. Second observation: the Oct-6 Claude audit already recorded that formalization.yaml lists no elliptic-curve manuscript (OPENAI_RELEASE_AUDIT.md:5), and sweep-lean.json finding 5 already recorded that the eleven lana-agents packages are declared, patched, imported by no OAI file, and absent from the clone — so Codex's L5 is ALREADY-COVERED as to location and NEW only in the declaration-level reading of five external files, which I confirm as accurate but narrower than its 'reuse' bullets. Third: the elliptic-curves README (5476 lines, sha 4e47c4c9...) is largely a changelog of docstring 'reach clause' repairs (e.g. lines 592-1016), i.e. this is an agent-generated library whose own documentation records repeated stale-hypothesis incidents; declarations, not docstrings, must be read, which Codex's DeterminantGeneral remark (FORMALIZATION_SCOPE.md:75) also illustrates.
